analysis.title: What we learned in Barcelona - Market Anxieties Outweigh Fundamentals
key_insights: Ten covered European semi companies attended MS's TMT Conference. Management tone was constructive with orders on track and pricing power evident, but share prices are not reacting positively.
Geopolitics weighs heavily on the sector. Most meetings spent considerable time on data centre build-out risks and potential export restrictions.
MS sees a clear disconnect between resilient business conditions and cautious investor sentiment. Industry View is In-Line.
MS continues to like ASML for its unique supply chain positioning and thinks it has the best chance of outperformance from here. Rating Overweight, PT €1,700 on 25x FY28 EPSe of €68.47.
Semi-cap: ASML and ASMI gave balanced commentary, acknowledging uncertainty on US legislation and export restrictions while citing business strength into 2027.
ASMI reiterated FY27 revenue above €5.7bn at constant currencies. Its outlook explicitly assumes no additional export controls.
VAT said revenue is moving towards CHF2bn, reinforcing confidence in backlog conversion.

China and the proposed MATCH Act are the principal overhangs, and investors want clarity on scope before underwriting growth. A defined legislative outcome around year-end could be a clearing event and help turn sentiment in early 2027.
Analog and optics: Infineon cited resilient AI data centre demand above its €4bn FY27 guide and rising content per kilowatt.
STMicro reiterated data centre revenue should more than double in 2027 from c.$1.3bn in 2026, with messaging suggesting c.$2.8bn next year.

Soitec stood out in photonics, reinforcing breadth of demand and accelerating capacity expansion. Higher power and optical content is a growth vector but leaves exposure to the pace of infrastructure spending.

Arm targets a 4x power efficiency improvement by 2030 and has firmer confidence in c.$2bn AGI CPU sales across FY27/28. Wafer commitments support the initial ramp, and further upside needs more supply.
Arm sees build-out plans largely intact through CY27 but acknowledges risk of delays thereafter. MS thinks Arm may launch a v10 architecture (2027?) focused on AI compute and security.

market_movers.rationale: Unique supply chain positioning and best chance of outperformance. PT is 25x P/E on €68.47 FY28 EPSe.

sector_views.rationale: Industry View In-Line. Fundamentals are strong but geopolitics and data centre build-out concerns cap sentiment.
Visibility into 2027 is strong but MATCH Act and export restriction risk keep the 2028 debate open.

earnings_insights: ASMI reiterated FY27 revenue above €5.7bn at constant currencies (company guidance).
Infineon AI data centre demand is above its €4bn FY27 guide (company commentary).
STMicro data centre revenue expected to more than double in 2027 from c.$1.3bn in 2026, with c.$2.8bn suggested (management messaging).
Arm expects c.$2bn AGI CPU sales across FY27/28 (management confidence).
risk_factors: Export controls and MATCH Act scope could hit equipment names.
Data centre build-out pace and possible delays after CY27.
ASML downside: weaker foundry/DRAM demand, inflation cycle and Chinese weakness driving order push-outs, absent High NA adoption in DRAM 2028+.
ASML upside risks: foundry/logic ramp, higher HBM/DRAM spend, servicing margins, tech sovereignty programmes.
vol_and_positioning: Investor sentiment is cautious and conviction on data centre spending is much weaker than management's, per MS.
geopolitical: Proposed US MATCH Act and potential export restrictions on semiconductor equipment, with China as a principal overhang.
Potential export restrictions and data centre build-out risks dominated meetings.

key_data_points.anchor: Applying a 25x P/E multiple to our €68.47 FY28 EPSe gives us a PT €1,700.

tension_points.bull_case: Orders on track, pricing power evident, and sales and margin progression in last quarter's prints, with visibility into 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Share prices are not responding as geopolitics, export restrictions and data centre build-out risk weigh, and investor conviction is much weaker than management's.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A defined MATCH Act outcome around year-end could clear the overhang. Conversely, data centre build-out delays beyond CY27 would break the bull case.
